lines: A function handles comparison difference between Paddle and Python.
For example, if x and y are Tensors, x.shape == y.shape will return single
boolean Value (True/False). However, paddle.shape(x) == paddle.shape(y) is
an element-wise comparison. The difference can cause dy2stat error. So we
create this function to handle the difference.
If the variables to compare are NOT Paddle Variables, we will return as
Python like "a op1 b and b op2 c and ... ".
If the variables to compare are Paddle Variables, we will do elementwise

lines: """Returns the value of $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, a directory path.
This directory is intended for 'user-specific non-essential runtime files
and other file objects (such as sockets, named pipes, ...)', and
As of late 2012, only quite new systems set $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. If it is not
set, with ``strict=True`` (the default), a KeyError is raised. With
``strict=False``, PyXDG will create a fallback under /tmp for the current
user. This fallback does *not* provide the same guarantees as the
specification requires for the runtime directory.
The strict default is deliberately conservative, so that application
developers can make a conscious decision to allow the fallback.

lines: """Iterate over the tree returning text nodes in a depth first fashion,
skipping text nodes inside certain tags.
# This is basically a stack that we extend using itertools.chain.
# This will either consist of an element to iterate over *or* a string
# If the element isn't meant for display, ignore it.
# el.text is the text before the first child, so we can immediately
# return it if the text exists.
# We add to the stack all the elements children, interspersed with
# each child's tail text (if it exists). The tail text of a node

cookie and include the same value as a non-cookie
field with all ``POST`` requests. If the two do not match, we
reject the form submission as a potential forgery.
The ``_xsrf`` value may be set as either a form field named ``_xsrf``
or in a custom HTTP header named ``X-XSRFToken`` or ``X-CSRFToken``
(the latter is accepted for compatibility with Django).
Prior to release 1.1.1, this check was ignored if the HTTP header
has been shown to be insecure and has been removed. For more

* allow_cell_edits - whether cells can be edited
* locked - which columns are locked to the left of the grid
* sort - The sort to apply to the data on startup (EX: [("col1", "ASC"), ("col2", "DESC"),...])

* background_mode - different background displays in grid
* range_highlights - specify background colors for ranges of values in the grid
* vertical_headers - if True, then rotate column headers vertically
* column_edit_options - the options to allow on the front-end when editing a cell for the columns specified
* highlight_filter - if True, then highlight rows on the frontend which will be filtered when applying a filter

* hide_shutdown - if true, this will hide the "Shutdown" button from users

* hide_main_menu - if true, this will hide the main menu from the screen
* hide_column_menus - if true, this will hide the column menus from the screen
* enable_custom_filters - if True, allow users to specify custom filters from the UI using pandas.query strings

lines: def getlength(self, text, mode="", direction=None, features=None, language=None):
Returns length (in pixels with 1/64 precision) of given text when rendered
in font with provided direction, features, and language.
This is the amount by which following text should be offset.
Text bounding box may extend past the length in some fonts,
e.g. when using italics or accents.
The result is returned as a float; it is a whole number if using basic layout.
Note that the sum of two lengths may not equal the length of a concatenated
string due to kerning. If you need to adjust for kerning, include the following
hello_world = hello + world # not adjusted for kerning
hello = font.getlength("HelloW") - font.getlength("W") # adjusted for kerning
hello_world = hello + world # adjusted for kerning
hello_world = hello + world # kerning is disabled, no need to adjust
:param mode: Used by some graphics drivers to indicate what mode the
driver prefers; if empty, the renderer may return either
mode. Note that the mode is always a string, to simplify
:param direction: Direction of the text. It can be 'rtl' (right to
left), 'ltr' (left to right) or 'ttb' (top to bottom).
:param features: A list of OpenType font features to be used during text
layout. This is usually used to turn on optional
font features that are not enabled by default,
for example 'dlig' or 'ss01', but can be also
used to turn off default font features for
to disable kerning. To get all supported
:param language: Language of the text. Different languages may use
different glyph shapes or ligatures. This parameter tells
the font which language the text is in, and to apply the
correct substitutions as appropriate, if available.
It should be a `BCP 47 language code
:return: Width for horizontal, height for vertical text.
return self.font.getlength(text, mode, direction, features, language) / 64
